item.text: I’m checking the project memory for the documented retrieval behavior of `get_relevant_context` so I can answer from the maintained source of truth rather than guessing.

content.text:
Relevant recorded knowledge (3 items):

• Constraint — "Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump"
  hasDescription: Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs, EXPAND_FROM_TOP/EXPAND_MAX_HOPS/EXPAND_MAX constants). Relational expansion in get_relevant_context is a budgeted reach to the few linked records that complete an answer — specifically the lexically-distant neighbor that BM25 alone misses — without dumping the full neighborhood. Concretely: expansion seeds from only the top-N BM25 hits (EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3), walks at most EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops outward, and appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total linked records. Context efficiency is the whole point of get_relevant_context: returning the entire reachable neighborhood would negate the retrieval tool's purpose of surfacing the most relevant records without overwhelming the caller's context window. Expansion is skipped entirely for list-all calls and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  hasTitle: Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-19T17:26:52Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Constraint/f28b0186-bd10-4b8c-b2d8-64c06b30f2da

• ArchitecturalDecision — "Benchmark oracle mode: harness-side retrieval isolates knowledge-value from fetch-willingness"
  hasDescription: Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/run.py`). A `mode="oracle"` parameter on `run_cell()` causes the harness to retrieve relevant knowledge and prepend it verbatim to the prompt, without giving the agent a live memory tool. This isolates two confounds: H8 (fetch-willingness — whether the agent chooses to call the memory tool) and knowledge-value (whether the knowledge itself helps). If oracle does not beat B0, the captured knowledge has no value; if live-tool < oracle, the gap is fetch-willingness alone.

Implementation: `oracle_context()` calls `get_relevant_context` for B2 (current-only, symbolic BM25); `freetext_oracle_context()` runs BM25 over the exported chunk file for B1 arms (currency-blind — superseded chunks are retrievable, same as what a B1-rag agent would get). Topic is `task["memory_topic"] or task["prompt"]` — a focused subject phrase so the retrieval signal is unambiguous.

Oracle asymmetry is intentional: the B2−B1 oracle delta isolates B2's currency-awareness (the agent acting on lifecycle status) rather than information withholding (B1 oracle would also retrieve superseded chunks, so if B2 oracle correctly ignores a superseded record and B1 oracle uses it, that gap is earned).
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  hasTitle: Benchmark oracle mode: harness-side retrieval isolates knowledge-value from fetch-willingness
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-19T19:27:46Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/49bde203-68f6-47ec-99c7-2e109ef88a62

• Lesson — "Don't index instance data for A-box recall — MOOSE walk planning beats vector search for precision and auditability"
  hasDescription: Commit 17bcfda8 / tasks/lessons.md addition. Pattern surfaced during investigation of `get_relevant_context` imprecision: the temptation was to improve recall quality via embedding-ranked A-box recall or embedding-based instance dedup — building a vector index over recorded instance content. This contradicts a deliberate MOOSE design choice: MOOSE deliberately does NOT index instance data; walk planning was devised to avoid the vector-index/RAG trap and deliver more precise, auditable retrieval.

Rule: when recall, dedup, or contradiction detection seems to need "semantic search" over recorded instances, reach for the symbolic path first — `query` (walk planning) and `sparql` for retrieval precision; LLM-as-sensor + typed conflict for contradiction — not a nearest-neighbor index over instances. Embeddings in MOOSEDev are confined to T-box term alignment (`suggest_parent`) over the static ontology (class placement, not instance retrieval). `get_relevant_context` is a shallow lexical anchor/browse tool by construction; fix its imprecision with an honesty floor + tool-selection guidance, not vector search.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/03d8d242-c154-4b55-8b3b-781289fbcb6c

item.text: `get_relevant_context` currently does a lexical BM25-style retrieval over the current working set, then optionally performs a bounded graph expansion from only the top 3 hits, walking up to 2 hops and appending at most 5 linked records. The project memory entry I relied on is **“Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump.”**
